title: Arterial pressure monitoring systems
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Device-neutral educational specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.

parameters.name: Arterial pressure value
parameters.explanation: An invasive measurement depends on a correctly referenced and functioning pressure system. Assess the patient and correlate an implausible value with an alternative measurement when feasible.

parameters.name: Arterial waveform
parameters.explanation: The trace represents pulsatile arterial pressure. Excessive damping may flatten the trace and underestimate systolic pressure; resonance can exaggerate the systolic peak. These distortions require trained assessment, not independent treatment changes.

parameters.name: Zero and levelling
parameters.explanation: Levelling relates the transducer to the intended anatomical reference; zeroing establishes the measurement baseline. A height or reference error may distort the pressure. Follow the specific system instructions and reassess after position changes.

safety_concepts.text: Keep all components of the pressure-monitoring system sterile (CDC Category IA).
Do not give dextrose-containing solutions or parenteral nutrition through the pressure-monitoring circuit (CDC IA).
Scrub the diaphragm with an appropriate antiseptic before accessing the system through a diaphragm (CDC IA).
Prefer a closed continuous-flush system and minimise manipulations and entries (CDC Category II).

Correlate the displayed arterial pressure with the patient's perfusion. If the reading is implausible, arrange a trained check of transducer level, zero reference, waveform quality and another pressure measurement under the unit protocol. Do not base treatment solely on a suspect reading.

Verify the pressure-system flush fluid against the approved arterial-line procedure and keep its label visible. Glucose-containing flush fluid can contaminate a sample and produce a falsely high glucose result even after discarding fluid. Escalate suspected contamination immediately and arrange an independent reliable glucose sample with the team before acting on the suspect result.

monitoring_concepts.text: Trend arterial pressure and waveform with the patient's perfusion; also monitor heart rate, limb perfusion, insertion site, flush system, alarms and ongoing line necessity according to local policy. ESICM 2025 supports arterial catheter monitoring for adult shock persisting despite initial therapy or requiring vasopressors. SSC 2026 conditionally allows invasive or noninvasive blood pressure monitoring in adult septic shock (very low certainty), with arterial monitoring particularly advised for substantial or escalating vasopressor support, multiple agents, frequent arterial sampling or repeatedly inconsistent cuff readings. The responsible team chooses the method; never delay urgent care solely to place a line.

escalation_concepts.text: Escalate immediately for bleeding or disconnection (apply pressure and call for help), a cold, pale or painful limb, loss of waveform with deterioration, suspected injection into the line or signs of infection. Do not delay help for an unstable patient while troubleshooting the trace.
